entries.subject: AC-2 design note: action-id registry, relay-write schema, session-token/CSRF
entries.text:
(a) Action-id registry. An action_id is issued only when the backend renders an executable-request card (GET /api/movements/<id>). It is sha256(canonical_json({movement_id, relay_file, operation, args, working_directory, source_relay_seq}))[:16], where operation is one of {route_to_engineer, record_decision, reject} and args is the exact local_relay.py append parameters (marker/subject/text/next/authorized_by/scope/supersedes) the button will submit verbatim -- never free-form text typed in the browser. source_relay_seq = len(relay_obj["entries"]) at issuance time, reusing the same signal orchestrator.py._status_row already computes for its REVISION_CHANGED_SINCE_DISPATCH check, rather than inventing a second staleness idea. Registry storage follows the existing runtime-bookkeeping pattern (outside the relay file, like orchestrator's own process records): one file per movement under NEXUS_ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_DIR, "<movement_id>.actions.json", mapping action_id to {operation, args, working_directory, source_relay_seq, issued_at, consumed_at, consumed_relay_seq}. On click: unknown id is 404; an already-consumed id is rejected (duplicate-click guard); the live relay file's current entry count is compared to source_relay_seq and a mismatch is rejected as stale (something was appended since the card was rendered -- a RELAY_CORRECTION or a newer decision). Only then does the backend call local_relay.py append with the registered args and record consumed_at/consumed_relay_seq from that call's result. local_relay.py's own content-hash optimistic-concurrency check (LOCAL_RELAY_PROTOCOL.md section 6) remains a second, independent guard at the actual write, not replaced by this registry.

(b) Relay-write schema. No new marker. LOCAL_RELAY_PROTOCOL.md section 4 states the seven-marker vocabulary is exactly closed; adding an eighth would violate that already-written contract and this AC's own instruction not to invent an incompatible file format. Every dashboard action maps onto an existing marker: a genuinely new PO decision (AMENDMENT case 2) becomes RELAY_DECISION with authorized_by/scope/supersedes populated from the session (authorized_by = the bearer-token session's identity, scope = "<movement_id> dashboard action", supersedes = the prior entry's seq if this replaces one, else "none"); an already-authorized auto-route or a queued message-box note (case 1, and the "send a note" field) becomes RELAY_NOTE -- factual status/instruction, never itself a new authority; a reject on a genuinely-new-decision card becomes RELAY_DECISION recording the decline, since declining is still a PO decision. Case 3 (platform/policy block) gets no write button at all -- there is nothing to append, only the real blocker text the card already shows. The action_id/operation metadata rides as plain, greppable text inside subject (e.g. "DASHBOARD_ACTION action_id=<id> op=<operation>") rather than as new JSON fields, so no schema change is needed anywhere -- the engineer session already reads relay entries as free text today (the standing ENGINEER_PROMPT instruction to act on RELAY_CORRECTION/RELAY_DECISION entries), exactly like every other entry.

(c) Session-token + Origin/CSRF. Reuses docs/design/OPERATOR_CONSOLE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 7.2's cookieless-bearer-token pattern directly, adapted to stdlib http.server since that document's fastapi/uvicorn stack is out of scope here per AC-6. The dashboard subcommand generates one secrets.token_urlsafe(32) per process launch, printed once to the terminal as http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#t=<token>; the frontend reads it from location.hash, strips it via history.replaceState, holds it only in memory, and sends it as an Authorization: Bearer header on every /api/* call. No cookie is ever set, so the ambient-credential class of CSRF is structurally impossible, the same reasoning that document already gives; Origin is still checked as defence in depth on every state-changing (PUT/POST) /api/* route -- rejected if present and not equal to http://127.0.0.1:<port> (absence is allowed, since the bearer token, not Origin, is the real authorization boundary). Server-side token comparison uses hmac.compare_digest, never ==. GET / and static assets stay unauthenticated (no evidence lives in them, matching that document's own rule); every /api/* route, read or write, requires the token. The token lives only in a module-level in-memory variable, regenerated on every dashboard invocation, never written to disk -- the same "runtime bookkeeping, not durable governance history" posture orchestrator.py's own state directory already uses.

Waiting for acknowledgment before starting AC-3 implementation, per this movement's merge_gate.
